examples.en: My grandfather cleared the foot of the mountain and made a field.
To clear wasteland, you have to pick out the stones first.

examples.ko: 사람들이 갯벌을 개간하는 일에 대해 이야기했어요.
examples.en: People talked about reclaiming the tidal flats.

examples.ko: 우리 가족은 십 년 동안 땅을 개간했어요.
examples.en: Our family cleared the land for ten years.
Clearing a forest affects the environment.

examples.ko: 마을 사람들이 함께 벌판을 개간하기 시작했어요.
examples.en: The villagers began clearing the field together.

explain: 주로 '땅을 개간하다', '황무지를 개간하다'처럼 목적어에 땅이나 들판이 와요. 새 길이나 분야를 여는 일에는 '개척하다'를 쓰니까 구별해서 써요.
explain_en: The object is usually land, as in '땅을 개간하다' or '황무지를 개간하다'. For opening up a new path or field, use '개척하다' instead.

examples.en: I looked at the place where the sky and sea meet.

examples.ko: 두 집의 담이 서로 맞닿아 있어요.
examples.en: The walls of the two houses touch each other.
My heart raced the moment our fingertips touched.

examples.ko: 우리 방은 옆집 벽과 맞닿고 있어서 소리가 잘 들려요.
examples.en: Our room shares a wall with the next house, so sounds carry easily.
Cups make a sound when they touch each other.

examples.ko: 책상 두 개를 맞닿을 만큼 가깝게 붙여 놓았어요.
examples.en: I put two desks so close that they touch.

explain: 둘이 서로 끝이 닿을 때 써서 '서로 맞닿다'처럼 자주 말해요. 한쪽이 상대에게 닿는 건 '닿다', 아예 붙어 버린 건 '붙다'를 써요. 소리는 [맏따타]로 나요.
explain_en: It is used when two things touch end to end, so '서로 맞닿다' (touch each other) is a common phrase. When only one side reaches the other, use '닿다'; when they are completely stuck together, use '붙다'. It is pronounced [맏따타].

examples.en: I worked at one workplace for half of my life.
My father has done nothing but farm for half of his life.

examples.ko: 반평생이 지나서야 제 꿈을 알게 됐어요.
examples.en: Only after half my life had passed did I realize what my dream was.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 우리 가족이 반평생 지켜 온 곳이에요.
examples.en: This shop is a place our family has kept going for half a lifetime.

examples.ko: 반평생 동안 고향을 떠난 적이 없어요.
examples.en: I haven't left my hometown in half my life.
I heard they donated the money they had saved for half their life.

explain: 정확히 몇 년이라는 뜻보다 '아주 오랜 세월'이라는 느낌으로 써요. 어른이 자기 삶을 돌아보며 말할 때 자주 나와요. 평생 전체를 말할 때는 '평생'을 써요.
explain_en: It conveys 'a very long time' rather than an exact number of years, and adults often use it when looking back on their lives. For the whole of a life, use '평생'.

examples.en: When the power went out, we turned on the generator.
At the campsite they use a small generator.
The hospital has an emergency generator.
The generator is too noisy.
The wind turbine generator is spinning in the wind.
At the construction site they make electricity with a generator.

explain: 전기를 만들어 내는 기계예요. '발전소'는 전기를 만드는 큰 시설, '발전기'는 그 안이나 캠핑·공사장에서 쓰는 기계라는 점이 달라요. 소리가 같은 '발전기(發展期)'는 발전해 가는 시기를 뜻하니 문맥으로 구별하세요.
explain_en: A machine that produces electricity. A '발전소' is a large power plant, while a 발전기 is the machine inside it or one used at campsites and construction sites. There is also a same-sounding 발전기 (發展期) meaning a period of development, so tell them apart by context.

examples.en: The advance party leaves first and prepares the lodging.
Our team's advance group arrived in the morning.

examples.ko: 저는 선발대로 먼저 가서 자리를 잡을게요.
examples.en: I'll go ahead as the advance party and grab a spot.
Try contacting the advance group.

examples.ko: 등산 갈 때 선발대와 후발대로 나눴어요.
examples.en: For the hike, we split into an advance group and a rear group.

examples.ko: 행사 선발대에 뽑혀서 하루 일찍 갔어요.
examples.en: I was chosen for the event's advance team, so I went a day early.

explain: 반대말은 '후발대'예요. 군대뿐 아니라 여행이나 행사에서 먼저 가서 준비하는 사람들에게도 써요. '선발'(뽑다)과 헷갈리기 쉬운데, 선발대의 '선'은 '먼저(先)'이고 선발(選拔)의 '선'은 '고르다'라서 한자가 달라요.
explain_en: The opposite is '후발대' (rear group). Besides the military, it is used for people who go ahead to prepare for trips or events. It is easy to confuse with '선발' (selection), but the '선' in 선발대 is 先 ('first'), while the '선' in 선발 is 選 ('choose'), so the Chinese characters differ.

en: the others; the rest; other (as a modifier)

examples.ko: 이 가게는 여타 가게보다 값이 싸요.
examples.en: This shop is cheaper than other shops.
We'll talk about the other issues tomorrow.
I'm good at English, but not at other foreign languages.
I'll tell you the remaining items separately.
The rest of the students have already gone home.
The rules are different in other cases.

explain: '여타'는 '그 밖의 나머지'를 말하고, 보통 명사 앞에서 '여타 + 명사'로 써요. '다른'보다 딱딱하고 글에 더 많이 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '나머지'나 '다른'을 써도 충분해요.
explain_en: '여타' means 'everything else' and is usually placed before a noun: '여타 + noun'. It is stiffer than '다른' and appears more in writing. In everyday talk, '나머지' or '다른' work fine.

examples.en: Our country has a long history.

examples.ko: 이 바위는 장구한 세월 동안 바람을 맞았어요.
examples.en: This rock has been exposed to the wind for a very long time.
That tradition has continued for a very long time.
Since the history is long, there is a lot to see.
This temple's history is truly long.
The long-running debate finally ended.

explain: '길다'와 달리 시간, 역사, 세월처럼 오랜 기간에만 쓰는 글말이에요. '장구한 역사', '장구한 세월'처럼 앞에서 꾸며 주는 꼴로 가장 많이 써요. 악기 '장구'와는 소리만 같고 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: Unlike '길다' (long), it is a written-style word used only for long spans of time, such as history and years. It is most often used before a noun, as in '장구한 역사' and '장구한 세월'. It sounds the same as the drum '장구' but is a different word.

p.n: 긴 is plain and ordinary; 장구한 sounds grand, literary, and ancient.
